content.text: {"primary_meaning":"A community that claims religious legitimacy or covenant identity but, through opposition to God, Christ, or faithful believers, functions as an instrument of Satan. In Christian interpretation, the expression usually signifies false or hostile religion rather than a building or an assembly openly dedicated to Satan.","primary_basis":["Revelation 2:9 — opponents of the church at Smyrna who claim to be Jews are called “a synagogue of Satan.”","Revelation 3:9 — the same designation is applied to opponents of the church at Philadelphia.","Psalm 26:5 — the psalmist declares hatred for the “assembly of evildoers” or “congregation of the wicked.”","John 8:39–44 — often cited in Christian interpretation as a parallel in which claimed covenant ancestry is contrasted with conduct characterized as doing the devil’s works.","Romans 2:28–29 — sometimes used to support the broader theological distinction between outward religious identity and inward faithfulness."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The phrase in Revelation refers specifically to local Jewish opponents of the Christian communities in first-century Smyrna and Philadelphia, probably in the context of social exclusion, denunciation, or persecution. On this reading it is historically particular and must not be generalized to Jews or Judaism.","basis":["Revelation 2:9","Revelation 3:9","The local and polemical settings of the messages to the seven churches"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"It symbolizes an apostate or false church: people professing to belong to God while corrupting doctrine, persecuting genuine believers, or serving worldly and demonic interests.","basis":["Revelation 2:9","Revelation 3:9","Matthew 7:15–23","2 Corinthians 11:13–15"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"It represents an end-times counterfeit religious system or organized anti-Christian power aligned with Satan.","basis":["Revelation 2:9","Revelation 3:9","Revelation 13:11–18","Revelation 17:1–6"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"It denotes ethnic Jews or Judaism generally as satanic or rejected by God.","basis":["A polemical generalization from Revelation 2:9 and 3:9"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"It refers literally to an assembly whose members consciously worship Satan.","basis":["A strictly literal reading of the phrase without regard to its polemical context"],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus about the expression’s rhetorical symbolism—an ostensibly legitimate religious body acting in opposition to God—but no full consensus about its precise historical or prophetic referent. Mainstream contemporary interpretation generally rejects applying “synagogue of Satan” to Jewish people or Judaism as a whole, emphasizing that Revelation addresses particular opponents in specific first-century cities."}
